title: National Museum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Windows, railings, shorelines and imagined gardens divide one kind of space from another.
introduction:
The railing in *The Scream* offers a firm diagonal through a world of wavering contours. Elsewhere, a balcony contains a quiet winter prospect, and a church doorway joins a dim interior to daylight. These boundaries are more than convenient parts of a setting. They establish where a figure stands, what can be reached, and how an outside world enters a picture.

This selection moves among Munch, Backer, the Krohgs, Kielland and several landscape and fairy-tale subjects. It does not ask every image to illustrate anxiety. A threshold may organise ordinary work or communal life just as effectively as it can intensify estrangement. The differences deserve as much attention as the recurring forms.
visitNote: These are selected works in the National Museum’s collection. They are distinct from works held by Oslo’s separate MUNCH museum. Check the National Museum’s current collection records for display, loans and any changes before planning a visit.

books.title: The Practice and Science of Drawing
books.author: Harold Speed
books.note: Speed’s chapters on tone, line and composition supply a practical vocabulary for comparing Backer’s illuminated interiors with Balke’s compressed landscapes. The book is a way into those differences, not evidence of direct influence.

works.title: The Scream
works.medium: Tempera and wax crayon on cardboard
works.credit: Edvard Munch, The Scream. National Museum, Oslo. Reproduction via Wikimedia Commons (PD-Art). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: The railing's straight line offers a route through the scene, but the sky and water refuse its stability. Munch brings their curves into a close relationship with the open-mouthed figure holding its head. Distress no longer seems confined to one body. The composition makes the surroundings participate, without requiring a literal claim that the landscape is producing an audible sound.

works.title: Madonna
works.credit: Edvard Munch. Madonna. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The sacred title meets a partly exposed body enclosed by dark hair and shadow. A red halo-like form adds to the unresolved relation between devotional reference and flesh. Munch's tilted head and suspended pose do not settle into a single familiar category. The ambiguity is grounded in what the image joins, rather than in a missing explanatory anecdote.

works.title: Rue Lafayette
works.credit: Edvard Munch. Street Lafayette. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/edvard-munch/street-lafayette-1891
works.description: The man on the balcony has a view of urban activity from which he remains physically separate. Far below, short coloured strokes make the street busy but prevent each passer-by from receiving a distinct account. Munch makes distance an organising condition of looking. The city becomes a field of movement beneath an observer who is comparatively still.

works.title: Spring
works.credit: Edvard Munch. Spring. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The bright window and moving curtain bring the outside close to the pale young woman and her older companion. Munch lets illness and care share a room with signs of renewed air. The contrast does not guarantee recovery. Brightness can alter the conditions around a vulnerable figure without resolving the condition the figure occupies.

works.title: Sister Inger
works.credit: Edvard Munch. Sister Inger. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The dark dress nearly joins the background, leaving the face and hands to establish the figure's position. Their unequal placement prevents those light areas from becoming a symmetrical emblem. Munch makes a portrait out of restrained differences within darkness. The limited setting concentrates the sitter's presence while giving little warrant for assigning her a particular private mood.

works.title: Blue Interior
works.credit: Harriet Backer. Blue Interior. Image credit: Harriet Backer; Source credit: hgEgkxpd_4iyCA at Google Cultural Institute , zoom level maximum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The red writing desk gives the cool room a distinct point of contrast, but Backer does not make the seated woman the only recipient of attention. Furnishings, pictures and intervals of light remain substantial subjects. The figure belongs to the room's arrangement. Colour connects her with a space whose interest does not depend entirely on what she might be thinking.

works.title: Christening in Tanum Church
works.credit: Harriet Backer. Christening in Tanum Church. Image credit: Harriet Backer; Source credit: HwFRac5hmtoV0w at Google Cultural Institute , zoom level maximum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The doorway joins bright outdoor figures to people already seated in the dim church. Backer describes a communal event through the spatial conditions that receive it. Successive openings make looking move inward and outward, rather than resting only on the ceremony named in the title. Architecture gives the gathering a sequence of approaches and places to wait.

works.title: By Lamplight
works.credit: Harriet Backer. By Lamp Light. Image credit: Harriet Backer; Source credit: OgEFw8dGHdBwQw at Google Cultural Institute , zoom level maximum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The lamp's reach and the woman's attention meet at the task. Hands and profile receive enough warm light to make the working posture clear, while much of the room stays subdued. Backer gives concentration a visible boundary. The surrounding darkness need not signify isolation; it also distinguishes useful light from space not immediately required by the activity.

works.title: A Japanese Lantern
works.credit: Oda Krohg. A Japanese Lantern. Image credit: Oda Krohg; Source credit: fwGBNpCfAiI86w at Google Cultural Institute , zoom level maximum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Warm artificial light hangs before the cooler water and trees beyond the opening. Oda Krohg makes two conditions coexist without blending them into a single atmosphere. The seated woman remains inside that meeting of lights. The threshold establishes a relationship between interior and evening rather than simply separating a room from its view.

works.title: Christian Krohg at the Easel
works.credit: Oda Krohg. Christian Krohg at the Easel. Image credit: Oda Krohg. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The sitter's attention stays with the canvas, leaving the viewer to see him from the side. Palette, chair and posture identify artistic work without the formality of a public studio portrait. Oda Krohg keeps the outdoor surroundings loose. The practical arrangement is enough to give the occupied body a clear place and purpose.

works.title: Soria Moria Palace
works.credit: Theodor Kittelsen. Soria Moria Palace. Image credit: Theodor Kittelsen; Source credit: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The golden towers are sharply available to sight, but mist hides the structure that would connect them to a reachable place. Kittelsen makes the destination visible and inaccessible at the same time. Its fairy-tale character depends partly on that missing approach. Brightness promises recognition while the concealed base prevents an ordinary understanding of how to get there.

works.title: The Ash Lad and the Fox
works.catalogueTitle: The Ash Lad and the Fox
works.credit: Theodor Kittelsen. The Ash Lad and the Fox. Image credit: Theodor Kittelsen; Source credit: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The boy and upright fox face one another in a woodland clearing, their pause giving the encounter a familiar social shape. Kittelsen needs little spectacular scenery to introduce the tale's impossibility. A recognisable path and the distance between two figures are enough. The unusual participant enters a setting whose scale otherwise remains plausible.

works.title: Winter on the Balcony
works.credit: Harald Sohlberg. Winter on the Balcony. Image credit: Harald Sohlberg; Source credit: Nasjonalmuseet for kunst, arkitektur og design. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The railing stays close and definite while the water and ground beyond offer little activity. Sohlberg makes the protected vantage point part of the landscape rather than removing it for an unobstructed prospect. The view belongs to someone at a boundary, not to an eye floating freely outdoors. Muted colour reinforces the separation without explaining it as one fixed emotion.

works.title: Stetind in Mist
works.credit: Peder Balke. Stetind in Mist. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The pointed peak is clearer than much of the terrain supporting it. Balke lets haze remove information so that a decisive outline can establish the mountain's presence. Dark shore and pale distance give it scale through contrast. The scene's force comes from selective definition, not from an equally detailed account of every part of a vast place.

works.title: Lighthouse on the Norwegian Coast
works.credit: Lighthouse on the Norwegian Coast. Peder Balke; Source credit: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: The lighthouse offers a thin upright against the broad movements of water and cloud. Its smallness makes the coast's turbulence easier to measure. Balke gives the building a legible pale form but little power to command its surroundings. A structure meant to assist navigation appears within conditions that are visibly larger than its reach.

works.title: Summer Night
works.credit: Kitty Lange Kielland. Summer Night. Image credit: Kitty Lange Kielland; Source credit: PwGtQgwyhKNSTw at Google Cultural Institute , zoom level maximum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Kielland sustains the evening through close tonal relationships rather than a spectacular point of light. Reeds, lilies and reflections introduce small differences across the water's edge. The scene asks for attention to those variations instead of a dramatic event. Stillness is not an absence of information; it changes the scale at which the information becomes worth following.

works.title: View over the Sea from Ogna, Jæren
works.catalogueTitle: View over the Sea from Ogna, Jæren
works.credit: Kitty Lange Kielland. View over the Sea from Ogna, Jæren. Image credit: Kitty Lange Kielland; Source credit: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Rounded rocks and shallow channels complicate the near ground before the eye reaches the open sea. Kielland makes that approach tangible through irregular surfaces and low vegetation. The horizon is comparatively simple, but the foreground refuses a quick passage. A coast can be understood from what lies close to the feet as well as from a distant prospect.

works.title: Balestrand
works.credit: Hans Gude. Balestrand. Image credit: Hans Gude. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Small figures and buildings establish a familiar scale at the shore before the mountains enlarge it. Gude separates the near rock, water and slopes into readable distances, with light distinguishing selected areas. The fjord is substantial without becoming shapeless magnitude. Habitation supplies a foothold from which the long passage across the landscape can be judged.

works.title: A Forest
works.credit: Lars Hertervig. A Forest. Image credit: Lars Hertervig; Source credit: EwG0W3HsCM_1KA at Google Cultural Institute , zoom level maximum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The foreground trees enclose much of the view, but a distant opening and pale band of cloud prevent complete closure. Hertervig distributes visibility unevenly. Attention has to negotiate dense masses before finding brightness beyond them, so the forest's tension belongs to the arrangement itself. No invented event in the woods is needed to explain that difficulty of access.

works.title: The Golden Age
works.credit: The Golden Age. WikiArt; Lucas Cranach the Elder. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Resting, dancing and bathing figures share a garden with animals and fruit trees. Cranach makes the imagined harmony concrete through different untroubled activities, then places a wall around it. The boundary deserves attention: this ideal world is visibly set apart. Its ease depends on an arranged enclosure, not on a claim to record ordinary life outside it.

closingSections.title: Follow a boundary
paragraphs: Choose a window, shore or railing and trace what changes across it. The exercise connects these works without making them illustrations of one national mood. This selection concerns the National Museum's collection, not the separate MUNCH collection or a fixed current hanging. Confirm particular works and access through the museum before visiting.
